set: B: one sheet of consecutive frames at each hit

issues.what: The flash and sharp sideways kick make the hit readable, but H and the surrounding deck show no clear physical response. The arrow snaps left and slides back almost to its starting pose, so the spark carries most of the impact.
issues.fix: On the flash frame, drive H briefly into its socket and send a small jolt through the deck. Give the arrow a sharp deflection and a short, damped settle rather than easing it back to its starting pose.

issues.where: first red Invalid email block over the right-hand keys, 0:32.13–0:32.43
issues.what: The block already covers the keys in the first frame, then creeps upward a little and holds. The sheet shows the warning clearly but not what struck what or when it landed.
issues.fix: Include the approach and first contact in the crop. Make the block stop sharply on the visible key, with brief key travel or a deck jolt on the same frame, then hold on the landed pose.

issues.where: center red block and the lower edge, 0:32.70–0:33.07
issues.what: The center block is already in place after a blurred glimpse of the arrow. The next block enters at the bottom edge before the sheet establishes a visible point of contact for either action.
issues.fix: Reframe or retime the sheet to follow the incoming block all the way to its strike surface, keeping the arrow and the receiving key visible through contact and recovery.

issues.where: lower Invalid email block over V–M, 0:33.23–0:33.60
issues.what: The lower block hovers over the keys, rises slightly, then holds. The exposed key edges do not appear to compress or rebound, so the movement reads as a sliding banner rather than a heavy block striking the keyboard.
issues.fix: Give the block a decisive approach and hard stop against the keys, show the key row react on that frame, and keep the final hold after a brief, tight settle.
